name: Molded Products Inc
old_description: Molded Products was founded in 1986, initially focused on providing rubber molded goods for the automotive aftermarket.
about:
Molded Products Inc was founded in 1986 in Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, initially supplying rubber molded goods to the automotive aftermarket. The company began as a focused rubber molding operation and has since expanded into a diversified custom molder serving a broad range of industrial markets.

Today the company specializes in compression molding, transfer molding, and rubber-to-metal bonding, supported by an in-house tool and die shop that designs and builds production and prototype molds. Its facility runs 22 hydraulic presses up to 600 tons, along with preforming equipment, finishing lines that include cryogenic deflashing, a paint center, and general machining capabilities. Operations run 24 hours a day, five days a week, enabling quick turnaround on urgent orders.

Molded Products serves industries including oil and gas, construction, fuel-cell seals, electrical, automotive aftermarket, aerospace, and air filtration. The business model centers on contract manufacturing, providing turnkey solutions from concept and blueprint through tooling to finished rubber components for both original equipment manufacturers and aftermarket suppliers.

The company emphasizes its ISO 9001:2015 certified quality management system, in-house tooling control, and round-the-clock production as key differentiators. It positions itself on delivering quality, timely, and cost-competitive rubber molded components, with the flexibility to handle hot jobs quickly.

name: Molding Products
old_description: Founded in 1978, Molding Products LLC, an operating business of IP Corporation, supplies sheet molding composites (SMC) to the growing compression molding industry. Today, the company remains focused on providing industry-leading, custom-formulated molding compounds for a wide variety of industries and applications.
about:
Molding Products LLC was founded in 1978 in South Bend, Indiana, as an operating business of IP Corporation. The company began by supplying sheet molding composites (SMC) to the growing compression molding industry and has remained focused on custom-formulated molding compounds for diverse applications.

The company produces sheet molding composites (SMC) and engineered thermoset materials, offering custom formulation, compounding, compression molding, prototype tooling, and quality testing. Its manufacturing facility in South Bend houses compression presses and a programmable logic control system for process monitoring. A team of technical specialists—including sales representatives, engineers, and quality managers—supports projects from early concept through post-production, though total headcount is not disclosed.

Molding Products serves industries including aerospace, automotive, communications, construction, electrical, heavy-duty truck, HVAC, industrial furniture, marine, pallets, sanitary, sporting goods, swimming pools, and transportation. Customers range from OEMs designing structural components to firms seeking Class A automotive surfaces, low-density parts, or flame-retardant materials.

The company differentiates itself by not competing with its customers—it does not offer custom molding—while providing strategic alliances for mold prototyping, presses, and contract manufacturing. Early involvement in concept development, combined with access to current resin technologies through its sister company Interplastic Corporation, allows Molding Products to deliver tailored formulations with minimal lead-time loss.

name: Moldrite Products Inc
old_description: We guarantee Quality as well as Customer Service to all of our valued customers. We offer 100%  Made in the USA products and labor. Valuing the American made product  is what this company was founded upon and still believes in today. Offering competitive pricing and value compared to  overseas  operations is what Moldrite Products strives for. Customer Service, and Quality and Integrity… Moldite Products.
about:
The company has been family-owned and operated for over 25 years, building its reputation on 100% U.S.-made products and labor. While a specific founding year is not disclosed, the business emphasizes its roots in American manufacturing and a philosophy of quality and integrity passed down through the family.

The shop specializes in plastic injection molding, running Milacron machines exclusively with clamping forces from 55 to 450 tons. It produces parts weighing 1.5 to 76 ounces and offers a full suite of services including mold design and construction, production molding, consulting, mold storage, and machine-shop support. Materials stocked range from commodity resins such as ABS and styrene to engineering grades like Cycoloy, Lexan, and Noryl, along with custom colors, UV-inhibited, and UL-approved formulations.

Moldrite serves a broad base of industrial and commercial customers, though the company does not publicly list specific industry verticals or named clients. Its capabilities in mold storage and secondary machining allow it to support programs that require long-term tooling management and quick-turn maintenance.

The company differentiates itself through a 100% satisfaction guarantee, round-the-clock customer service, and a commitment to competitive pricing against overseas alternatives. Its OSHA-compliant production floor and secure mold-storage area underscore a focus on operational reliability and domestic supply-chain security.

name: Montana Specialty Mills
old_description: At Montana Specialty Mills, we process and market high quality oilseeds and specialty products. We adhere to rigorous standards in crop sourcing, processing operations, and customer service. Working directly with local growers ensures consistent access to the best production inputs. Our oilseed products are used as ingredients in a variety of foods that ultimately make their way to families’ kitchens across North America and beyond.
about:
Montana Specialty Mills operates from Great Falls, Montana, and has been processing oilseeds since 1997. The company was formed as a joint venture between Columbia Grain International, a global grain and pulse supplier headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and Nisshin OilliO America, part of a Japanese edible-oil manufacturing group. The partnership was created to serve regional growers and food manufacturers with consistent, high-quality oilseed ingredients.

The mill processes and markets organic and non-GMO oilseeds, turning crops sourced directly from growers in the northern U.S. and Canada into ingredients used by bakeries, food-service suppliers, repackers, and industrial food manufacturers. Its facilities are described as state-of-the-art, though specific square footage, headcount, or annual throughput are not disclosed.

End-use customers span the North American food supply chain, including commercial bakeries, food-service distributors, repacking operations, and manufacturers of prepared foods and industrial products. On the supply side, the company maintains long-term growing programs with a network of farmers, offering contracted acres and reliable settlement.

Montana Specialty Mills emphasizes rigorous standards in crop sourcing, processing, and customer service. Direct grower relationships are cited as the foundation for consistent input quality, while customers highlight the firm’s flexibility, reliability, and product consistency as key differentiators.

name: Montebello Plastics
old_description: Montebello Plastics specializes in high-quality polyethylene film solutions designed for a variety of
about:
Montebello Plastics, a small business based in Montebello, California, was founded in 2019. Co-founder Nado Husa leads the company alongside Chief Operating Officer Edward Lindgren and marketing head Chineze Afamefuna. The firm emphasizes over four decades of combined experience in plastic film extrusion.

The company manufactures custom polyethylene film products, including high-density (HDPE), low-density (LDPE), and linear low-density (LLDPE) films, as well as post-consumer recycled (PCR) and reprocessed materials. It operates as a made-to-order extrusion shop, producing poly bags, tubing, and sheeting in various sizes, thicknesses, and colors without holding any stock inventory. Specialty offerings include nano-enhanced films and a bioremediation technology designed to break down to zero micro plastics. All scrap generated during production is recycled.

Montebello Plastics serves the construction, industrial packaging, and agricultural sectors, along with customers in laundry and cleaners supply and general packaging. Referenced clients include Laundry & Cleaners Supply, Continental Western Corporation, and AMZ Packaging. The company ships nationwide and provides local truck delivery throughout the Inland Empire, Orange County, Los Angeles, and the San Fernando Valley.

The company differentiates itself through professional, responsive service and a commitment to sustainability. Its films are 100% recyclable and comply with California’s SB54 packaging requirements. Montebello Plastics also offers FDA-approved films and free shipping on U.S. orders over $50.

name: Monterey Mills
old_description: Sliver knitting, or high-pile knitting, is a process that locks individual fibers into a lightweight knit backing. The length of acrylic fibers used adds dimension and warmth to the fabric, when needed, without adding additional weight. Other advantages of using acrylic fibers include the incorporation of colorfast dyes and, a finished fabric that is odor and mildew resistant. The end result is a light, soft, comfortable fabric that is warmer than fleece and is machine washable and dryable.
about:
Monterey Mills operates from Janesville, Wisconsin. The company traces its current ownership to February 1995, when Dan Sinykin purchased the former Roller Fabrics after spending seven months working there without pay to evaluate the business. Sinykin, a former Procter & Gamble sales executive and founder of the Tailor’s Touch retail chain, assembled a management team, consolidated multiple plants, and expanded the product line into automotive, equestrian, apparel, hospital, and pet markets.

The mill specializes in sliver knitting — also called high-pile knitting — a labor‑intensive process that locks individual acrylic fibers into a lightweight knit backing. The technique yields fabrics that are warmer than fleece, odor‑ and mildew‑resistant, and machine washable. An in‑house R&D team controls fiber and yarn selection, pile height, density, tensile strength, width, color, and stitch count to develop performance fabrics for diverse applications. The company also produces blankets, bedding, and medical and pet products, all manufactured in the United States.

Customers span medical, pet, automotive, equestrian, apparel, and hospital sectors, as well as the blanket and bedding market. The firm’s technical capabilities allow it to tailor fabric specifications for OEMs and brand owners seeking custom performance textiles.

Monterey Mills positions itself as one of the few remaining U.S. practitioners of sliver knitting, a craft many competitors abandoned due to its complexity. The company emphasizes continuous improvement, domestic production, and sustainability — sourcing recycled raw materials, repurposing all production waste, and treating and reusing wastewater.

name: Montrose Molders
old_description: Montrose has been in business since 1966, is ISO9001 certified, and has a large and broad injection molding fleet.
about:
Montrose Molders operates from Piscataway, New Jersey, where it was founded in 1966 by William Bruce Wilson. The company began as a 22-person tool shop producing tight-tolerance molds for the plastics industry. In 1972, the addition of its first injection molding press set the direction for future growth. Today, the business remains family-owned, led by the Wilson family, now in its fourth generation of plastics manufacturing.

The firm functions as a vertically integrated custom plastics manufacturer. Its facility houses 51 injection molding machines ranging from 40 to 1,000 tons of clamp force, two extrusion lines with co-extrusion capability, and an on-site tool and die shop that builds both aluminum and steel molds. A 25,000-square-foot assembly area runs up to five lines simultaneously, supporting decoration, assembly, and packaging. Engineering services include mold flow simulation via Solidworks Plastics and industrial design to translate concepts into 3D models.

Montrose serves a range of sectors including automotive, aerospace, medical devices, electronics, lighting, safety, battery, retail, and consumer goods. Customers engage the company for contract injection molding, extrusion, tooling, and full assembly programs, relying on its one-stop-shop model from design through finished product shipment.

The company emphasizes its family legacy and a culture of quality, consistency, and value. Each client is assigned a dedicated project manager to oversee complex projects from concept to delivery. Montrose highlights its ISO 9001:2015 certification and a focus on shortening lead times and reducing costs as core differentiators.

name: More Than A Bakery
old_description: Delivering high-quality food manufacturing solutions and fostering our community since 1855.
about:
More Than A Bakery operates from Versailles, Kentucky, as part of a family-owned contract manufacturing group tracing its roots to 1855 in Richmond, Indiana.

The company produces cookies, crackers, and custom crumb and coating products for food service suppliers. Its capabilities include custom crumb and coating formulation, dessert crumb and coating production, R&D and product development, and product scale-up services. Finished goods can be packaged in bag-in-a-box, kraft bags, or super sacks.

Primary customers are food service suppliers and other food manufacturers seeking contract production of baked goods and coating ingredients. The company emphasizes its ability to support product development from concept through commercial scale.

The ownership describes its mission as creating a workplace that gives back to families and the community, guided by values labeled La Familia, Passion, Gratitude, Purposeful Growth, and Integrity. The group positions itself as a partner that balances business performance with employee well-being and community outreach.

name: Moriden America, Inc.
old_description: Moriden America, Inc. was founded in the United States in 1988 and began operations in Detroit Michigan in 1989. Our company opened operations in Indianapolis a year later, and in 1993 moved all operations to Indianapolis, Indiana.
about:
Moriden America, Inc. was established in 1988 as a U.S. subsidiary of Japan's Moriden Company LTD, which has over 80 years of experience in automotive, transportation, and furniture industries. Today it is headquartered in Carmel, Indiana, led by Vice President Minoru Sudo.

The company designs, develops, and manufactures automotive interior components across three main product lines: seating materials, interior trim, and cargo systems. Its capabilities include compression molding of coated carpets with soft trim and hardware, and an integrated production line for HS-RIM (high-strength reaction injection molding) cargo floor boards that minimize weight and maximize strength. Product offerings range from trunk trim parts and shift boots to upholstery, mat floors, rear seat backs, and tonneau covers.

Moriden America serves the automotive industry, supplying decorative and functional interior trim components to vehicle manufacturers and tier suppliers. Its seating materials, interior trim, and cargo systems are designed to meet the quality, safety, and delivery requirements of automotive programs.

The company emphasizes continuous improvement in safety, quality, cost, delivery, and management, tailoring processes to each project as a key differentiator. It also highlights end-to-end service from development proposal through design, production, quality control, logistics, and sales.

name: Moulstown Woodworks
old_description: Moulstown Woodworks is nestled in the Pigeon Hills of York County just east of Abbottstown, PA and from our log yard we take the portable sawmill service anywhere. Our motto is “can mill, will travel” which runs on the back of a 2021 Woodmizer LT40, fully hydraulic, commercial portable sawmill with a wide saw head that clears a 34” cut and up to 20’ log lengths.
about:
Moulstown Woodworks operates from a log yard in the Pigeon Hills of York County, just east of Abbottstown, Pennsylvania. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, but the business centers on a mobile sawmilling service that travels to client sites across Pennsylvania and Maryland.

The core service is on-site sawmilling: a 2021 Woodmizer LT40 hydraulic portable sawmill with a 34-inch cut capacity and 20-foot log length capacity is transported to the job site. The mill can handle logs up to 4,000 pounds; heavier logs require crane assistance. Typical output runs 250–300 board feet per hour, with service charges around $0.38–$0.42 per board foot for an eight-hour day, plus a transportation and setup fee starting at $85 within 10 miles of the Pigeon Hills.

The company serves a network of arborists, excavators, forestry consultants, lumber distributors, kiln operators, crane services, furniture makers, framing carpenters, cabinet shops, and luthiers across Adams, Cumberland, Perry, Lancaster, Chester, and York counties in Pennsylvania, as well as Frederick, Carroll, Baltimore, and Hartford counties in Maryland.

The company emphasizes a 'can mill, will travel' approach, stressing that proper site preparation—clean, metal-free logs staged for setup, adequate labor to clear slabs and lumber, and equipment to move heavy logs—enables the highest yield and efficiency.
